method: Read-only SQL through the Supabase connector. The same catalogue query ran on production and on a disposable database (the 408-migration history plus the merged 20270330090000 file); entries are key=value strings aggregated by md5(string_agg(... ORDER BY key)) per category. Functions: md5(pg_get_functiondef)|prosecdef|proconfig|sorted proacl. Tables: relrowsecurity|relforcerowsecurity|sorted relacl. Policies: md5(cmd|roles|permissive|qual|with_check). Triggers: md5(pg_get_triggerdef). Columns: type|notnull|default|sorted attacl. Constraints: md5(pg_get_constraintdef)|convalidated. Indexes: md5(indexdef). Scope: the 38 functions the migration creates or replaces and every object on the 14 tables it creates or alters.

table.explained: Row by row, RLS (on, not forced) and every grant are equal on all 14 tables. The only difference is the owner's ACL: postgres=arwdDxtm on production versus postgres=arwdDxt on the disposable database. The m (MAINTAIN) privilege is granted to the owner by Postgres 17 on every hosted table; it is not created by the migration and grants nothing to a client role.

data.note: Counts only; no row content and no personal data was read.

notVerified: No authenticated behavioural probe against production and no request in the hosted application runtime. Behaviour is covered by supabase/tests/security_work_supplier_cycle_test.sql (78 assertions), 22 negative controls, the two-connection race test and the PostgREST pilot on disposable databases. No sharing right is granted and nothing is sent externally.
writes: None. No production write, migration replay or activation.
